question.worked_solution:
Notice that the leading coefficient is negative. To reduce the expression to a more familiar form, we can factor out $-1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{x}^{2}-\frac{4}{5}x-\frac{1}{25} & = \\ -(4{x}^{2}+\frac{4}{5}x+\frac{1}{25})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the quadratic expression inside the parentheses using the square of a sum formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+\frac{4}{5}x+\frac{1}{25} & = \\ (2x)^{2}+\frac{4}{5}x+{(\frac{1}{5})}^{2} & = \\ (2x)^{2}+2\cdot (\frac{1}{5}\cdot 2x)+{(\frac{1}{5})}^{2} & = \\ {(2x+\frac{1}{5})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-(4{x}^{2}+\frac{4}{5}x+\frac{1}{25}) & = \\ -{(2x+\frac{1}{5})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$
